# Wen Programming Language

> Wen is an experimental, Python-inspired programming language with an LLVM-based compiler that generates native executables.

## Official Resources

Homepage: https://lampard1189-hub.github.io/Wen-Script/
Documentation: https://lampard1189-hub.github.io/Wen-Script/docs/
GitHub: https://github.com/lampard1189-hub/Wen-Script
PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/wen-lang/
Examples: https://github.com/lampard1189-hub/Wen-Script/tree/development/v0.2/examples

## Overview

Wen is an open-source experimental programming language.

Its compiler uses lexical analysis, parsing, semantic analysis, LLVM IR generation and Clang native compilation.

Current version: 0.2.0a1 (experimental alpha).

## Installation

    python3 -m pip install wen-lang==0.2.0a1

Requirements:
- Python 3.10 or newer.
- LLVM Clang available on the system.

## Language Features

- Variables declared with let.
- Strings, numbers and Boolean values.
- Print statements.
- Arithmetic and comparison operators.
- if and else conditional statements.
- while loops.
- Function definitions, parameters, calls and return statements.
- Comments beginning with #.
- Newline and semicolon statement separation.

## Compiler Architecture

1. Lexer: converts source characters into tokens.
2. Parser: builds an abstract syntax tree.
3. Semantic Analyzer: performs semantic checks.
4. LLVM Code Generator: produces LLVM intermediate representation.
5. Clang: generates the native executable.

## Project Status

Wen 0.2.0a1 is an experimental alpha release. Features and compiler behaviour may change.
